The [embedpdf](https://github.com/jmgirard/embedpdf) extension adds a `{{< pdf >}}` shortcode for embedding PDF files in your Quarto HTML documents and RevealJS presentations. On desktop it uses the browser's built-in PDF viewer; on mobile — where embedded PDFs normally fail to render — it automatically falls back to [PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/) so your readers see the document either way. This guide walks through the available options.

## Simple Usage

All you really need to give the `pdf` shortcode is the path to the PDF file you want to embed.

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf >}}

::: {.callout-important}
Remember to list the PDF file under `resources` in your document's YAML header (or under `project: resources:` in `_quarto.yml`) so that Quarto copies it into your output site alongside the HTML.
:::

## Customization

In most cases you will want to customize the appearance of the embedded PDF. A few common options are built into the shortcode for convenience; for anything more, pass a CSS `class` and style it yourself.

### Embed with width in pixels

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf width=600 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf width=600 >}}

### Embed with width in percent

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf width=100% >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf width=100% >}}

### Embed with height in pixels

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf height=600 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf height=600 >}}

### Embed with both width and height

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf width=600 height=400 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf width=600 height=400 >}}

### Embed with a 1px border

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf border=1 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf border=1 >}}

### Embed with a CSS class

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf class=myclass >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf class=myclass >}}

### Add a download button

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf button="Download PDF" >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf button="Download PDF" >}}

## Supporting Mobile Browsers

Mobile browsers (e.g., Chrome and Firefox on Android) do not support the inline rendering of PDF objects: they show a blank box or a download prompt instead. To solve this, the extension includes a JavaScript-based PDF renderer, [PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/).

By default (`renderer=auto`), each embedded PDF checks whether the browser can display PDFs inline (via `navigator.pdfViewerEnabled`). If it can, the browser's native PDF viewer is used. If it cannot, as on Android, PDF.js draws the PDF page by page. The PDF.js viewer has a small toolbar for zooming, page tracking, and downloading. iPhone and iPad are the exception to the `pdfViewerEnabled` check. Safari there reports that it can display PDFs, but users report that older iOS versions show only the first page. For this reason, `renderer=auto` always uses PDF.js on iPhone and iPad. A browser fetches the PDF.js library only for a PDF.js embed. Desktop visitors with a built-in PDF viewer fetch it only for `renderer=pdfjs` embeds.

### Force the PDF.js renderer

Set `renderer=pdfjs` to always use PDF.js.

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=pdfjs height=500 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=pdfjs height=500 >}}

::: {.callout-tip}
Forcing `renderer=pdfjs` on your desktop is the easiest way to preview exactly what your mobile visitors will see, without needing a phone.
:::

### Force the native renderer

Set `renderer=native` to always use the browser's built-in viewer.

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=native height=400 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=native height=400 >}}

In Safari on iPhone and iPad, `renderer=native` shows the PDF in Safari's own viewer. This was checked on 2026-10-18 in iOS 27.0 iPhone and iPad simulators and an iOS 27.1 iPhone simulator. In the iOS 27.1 iPhone simulator, a swipe inside the embed reached every page.

::: {.callout-note}
Self-contained documents (`embed-resources: true`) need no other file. The PDF and, for `auto` and `pdfjs` embeds, PDF.js are inside the one HTML file. See [selfcontained_test.html](selfcontained_test.html) for a self-contained page. If a PDF.js embed in a self-contained document cannot show its PDF, it says so and gives a "Download the PDF" link. The link saves the PDF under its file name. If the browser cannot decode the PDF inside the page, the embed shows the message with no link, with any renderer. See [selfcontained_failed_test.html](selfcontained_failed_test.html). The README "Known limitations" section lists where this was checked and what happens with JavaScript disabled.
:::

### Hide the PDF.js toolbar

`{{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=pdfjs toolbar=false height=400 >}}}`

{{< pdf sample.pdf renderer=pdfjs toolbar=false height=400 >}}

### Setting defaults for the whole document or project

You can set default values for any shortcode option under the `embedpdf` key in your document YAML header or `_quarto.yml`, so you don't have to repeat them:

```yaml
embedpdf:
  renderer: pdfjs
  height: 600
```

## PDFs on Another Site

You can give the shortcode the URL of a PDF on another site:

`{{{< pdf https://example.com/report.pdf >}}}`

This section is about pages that are not self-contained. On desktop, `renderer=auto` uses the browser's built-in viewer, so this section is about PDF.js embeds. `renderer=auto` uses PDF.js on iPhone and iPad and in browsers with no built-in PDF viewer, such as Chrome on Android. `renderer=pdfjs` uses PDF.js everywhere.

With PDF.js, your page reads the PDF itself. To let your page read a PDF from another site, the browser needs that site to allow the read with an `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. The checks named at the end of this section used only the value `*`.

Without the header, the embed shows "This PDF cannot be shown here." and an "Open the PDF" link. The link opens the PDF in a new tab.

On 2026-10-18, `curl -I` showed `access-control-allow-origin: *` for [https://jmgirard.github.io/embedpdf/sample.pdf](https://jmgirard.github.io/embedpdf/sample.pdf), a file on GitHub Pages. On the same date, `https://nbviewer.org/github/jhelvy/cv/blob/main/cv-jph.pdf` sent no such header.

To avoid the problem, put the PDF in your Quarto project and list it under `resources` in the YAML header. Then give the shortcode its relative path, for example `{{{< pdf cv.pdf >}}}`. If a script makes the PDF somewhere else, copy it into the project before you render.

A page can show one PDF from another site in two embeds, one with `renderer=native` and one with PDF.js. Safari refuses the PDF.js read of an address that a native embed on the page loaded, even with the header. So in this case only, the PDF.js embed reads the PDF at the same address with `embedpdf=pdfjs` added to its query. The site must answer that address with the same PDF. This was checked only on the local test servers.

These cases were checked on 2026-10-18 in Chromium with an emulated iPhone and an emulated Android phone. Android was checked by emulation in Chromium, not on a device. iPhone and iPad were checked only in Safari in iOS 27.0 simulators. The site sent no header on 2026-10-18 and sent `*` on 2026-10-19.

The case of a native embed and a PDF.js embed of one PDF was checked on 2026-10-19 with a site that sends `*`. It was checked in Safari in iOS 27.0 iPhone and iPad simulators, in desktop Safari 27.0.1, and in Chromium. A PDF of 14 pages and 171 KB then loaded in parts (by byte ranges). This was checked in the iOS simulators, and in Chromium with an emulated iPhone and Android phone. Desktop Safari was not checked for byte ranges.

## When JavaScript is Disabled

The viewer requires JavaScript to run. If a visitor has JavaScript disabled, the embedded PDF is replaced by a simple hyperlink to download the file. Adding a download button (`button="..."`) gives those visitors a clearer call to action.
